hotkeyConflict.title: Some hotkeys could not be registered:
hotkeyConflict.help: — already used by another app (Discord, NVIDIA, …). Change them in Settings → Hotkeys.
diagnostics.create.help: Saves one .zip on your Desktop with the logs, your settings and a description of this PC, then opens the folder so you can attach it. Nothing is uploaded, and it contains no screenshots and no map images.

update.manual.help: Asks GitHub Releases right now — the same single request as the startup check, made only when you press this. It works even when the switch above is off, and it does not turn it back on.
update.manual.foundUnknown: A newer version was found — downloading…
update.manual.upToDate: You are on the latest version ({version}).
update.manual.upToDateUnknown: You are on the latest version.

update.manual.devBuild: Not available in a development build.
update.manual.portableBuild: The portable version does not update itself — download the new one from the releases page.

settings.title: Settings
settings.language.help: Applies straight away — no restart. Map and creator names are never translated.
settings.minimizeToTray.help: Closing or minimizing the window keeps the app running in the system tray instead of quitting.
settings.hideFaqPopup.help: Stops the borderless-windowed reminder showing on startup.
settings.hardwareAcceleration: Use the graphics card to draw the app
settings.hardwareAcceleration.help: Off by default, to save memory: the overlay is a still image, so there is nothing for the graphics card to do. Turn it on if the app looks or feels wrong on your machine. Takes effect the next time the app starts.
settings.hardwareAcceleration.restart: Saved — it takes effect the next time the app starts.
settings.unloadWindowInTray: Free this window's memory in the tray
settings.unloadWindowInTray.help: On by default: while the app sits in the tray this window is closed to give its memory back — about a quarter of everything the app uses. The overlay, the hotkeys and automatic detection all carry on. Opening the window again takes a moment; turn this off to keep it instant.
settings.hideInMenu: Clear the map back in the menu
settings.hideInMenu.help: Only with Auto-detect map on: when the game returns to its main menu the match is over, so the overlay clears itself. The next Tab press detects the map again, even the same one.
settings.checkForUpdates.help: One HTTPS call to GitHub Releases at startup to see whether a newer version of the app exists. Turn this off to stop the check completely.
settings.checkForMapPacks.help: The app's other network request: one HTTPS call to GitHub, at most once a day, asking whether new or corrected map images exist. New maps then arrive as a few hundred KB instead of a whole app update. Nothing about you is sent, and with this off no request is made.
settings.mapPacks.none: No downloaded maps — you have the ones that ship with the app.
settings.mapPacks.installed: {count} downloaded map(s) on top of the ones that ship with the app.
settings.openLogFolder.help: If auto-detect misbehaves, open this folder and send detector.log — it records what the detector decided (map, score, timing), never any image.
settings.openLogFolder.failed: The log folder could not be opened.
settings.error.writeFailed: That change could not be saved — it will be lost when the app restarts.
settings.overlay.previewNotice: While this tab is open a preview image is shown on the overlay. Changes here apply to it directly.
settings.monitor.label: Display {index} ({width}x{height})
settings.glide.help: 0 is the left/top edge of the screen, 100 the right/bottom edge.
settings.mapLabel.help: Shown at the bottom of the overlay, never rotated with the map, at the same opacity. The OBS window follows the same setting.
settings.waylandWarning: This session runs on Wayland, where dragging the overlay does not work. Use the fine-grain position sliders instead.
settings.placeByHand: To place the overlay by hand: show a map, press Set position, drag the overlay with the mouse, then press Stop setting position.
settings.setPositionWarning: Forgetting to stop setting position leaves the overlay catching your mouse clicks in game.
settings.markers.help: Every marker is a possible location — the game switches a different subset on each match. On the maps that ship with the app the cellar, gate and car rings are already drawn on the image, so only the gas cans are added.
settings.tabMarkers.enabled: Draw them on the game's own map
settings.tabMarkers.help: While you hold Tab the game shows a big map with an arrow marking where you are. With this on, the markers are drawn straight onto that map, in the game's own scale, and disappear the moment you let go. The corner overlay keeps working exactly as before.
settings.tabMarkers.needsDetect: This needs Auto-detect map, which is switched off. The markers can only be placed once the app knows which map you are playing.
settings.tabMarkers.hideMinimap.help: If the game's own map is all you need, the corner overlay stays off screen for as long as this mode is running. It comes back by itself whenever this mode cannot run — for example with Auto-detect map switched off.
settings.tabMarkers.instant: Show them the moment I press the key
settings.tabMarkers.instant.help: After the app has seen the map once in a match, the markers fade in together with the game's map instead of waiting for the app to see it on screen. If you press the key where the map does not open — the chat, the pause menu — you may see a faint flash of markers for about half a second. Switch this off to always wait: nothing can flash, and the markers appear about a third of a second later.
settings.tabMarkers.mapKey.help: Whatever key opens the map in your game — Tab unless you rebound it. Press the button, then the key: one key on its own, no Ctrl/Alt/Shift, and mouse buttons cannot be used. When you switch this mode on the app checks once that Windows lets it ask at all — that check reads no key. After that, while the game is running, it asks Windows which program owns the window you are working in and — only when that is the game — whether that one key is held right now. It never receives, records or sees any other key, and it does not reserve this one, so the game still gets every press.
settings.tabMarkers.mapKey.error.withMod: One key on its own, with no Ctrl, Alt or Shift.
settings.tabMarkers.mapKey.error.unsuppo: That key cannot be used. Mouse buttons are not supported.
settings.tabMarkers.pollingOnly: Do not read the key state
settings.tabMarkers.pollingOnly.help: Uses only the slower method, which looks at the game's window a few times a second instead of asking about your map key. The feature still works; the markers take a little longer to appear.
settings.tabMarkers.method.key: Using your map key ({key}) — the markers appear as soon as you press it.
settings.tabMarkers.method.waiting: Ready — your map key ({key}) will be used as soon as the game is running. Nothing is being read in the meantime.
settings.tabMarkers.method.polling: Using the slower method, because you asked for it above.
settings.tabMarkers.method.unavailable: Using the slower method: reading the key state is not available on this PC. Everything still works, the markers just take a little longer to appear.
settings.tabMarkers.method.windowed: Not drawing: the game's window has a border or title bar, so the markers would sit slightly off on its map. Set the game to Borderless Windowed. The corner overlay is unaffected.
tabMarkers.fallback: Markers on the in-game map: using the slower method — reading your map key is not available on this PC. Everything still works.
markers.legend.note: A different subset is active each match.
onboarding.title: Welcome tour
onboarding.reopen.help: The short tour from the first start: language, where the map goes, what the markers mean, the hotkeys and auto-detect. It changes the same settings as this window.
onboarding.welcome.title: Welcome
onboarding.welcome.body: This app puts the map you are playing on top of the game, in a corner you choose, and lets you hide it or switch maps with a keyboard shortcut. A few short steps and you are set — you can skip them and change everything later under Settings.
onboarding.placement.title: Where the map goes
onboarding.placement.body: Pick the screen, the corner and how big the map should be. Its opacity, rotation and a finer position are under Settings → Overlay, and you can also drag it into place by hand.
onboarding.placement.preview: A sample map is on the overlay right now, so you can see exactly where it lands while you change these.
onboarding.placement.dragging: The corner is fixed while Overlay draggable is on — you are placing the overlay by hand. Switch that off under Settings → Overlay to pick a corner again.
onboarding.markers.title: What the markers mean
onboarding.markers.body: The overlay marks where the game may put the ways out and the gas cans — never where they are. A different subset is active each match, so read a marker as "worth checking".
onboarding.markers.bundled: The ways out are already drawn on the map images; the yellow gas-can markers are the ones this app adds. Each kind has its own switch under Settings → Overlay.
onboarding.hotkeys.title: Your hotkeys
onboarding.hotkeys.body: These are the combinations the app starts with. Every one of them can be changed, or switched off entirely, under Settings → Hotkeys — and each map has its own number key.
onboarding.hotkeys.gameOnly: They are reserved only while Halloween: The Game — or this window — is in front, so the rest of the time those combinations still belong to your other programs.
onboarding.hotkeys.tryIt: Try it: press {toggle} right now. This window counts as being in the game, so it works from here.
onboarding.hotkeys.tryIt.unbound: Show / hide has no combination at the moment. You can give it one under Settings → Hotkeys.
onboarding.hotkeys.tryIt.taken: {toggle} is already reserved by another program on this PC, so pressing it never reaches this app. Give it a different combination under Settings → Hotkeys.
onboarding.hotkeys.tryIt.ok: That was it — the shortcut reached the app.
onboarding.detect.title: Let it follow the game
onboarding.detect.body: With this on, press <kbd>Tab</kbd> in game once at the start of a match: the overlay switches to the map you are playing and names it for a few seconds. It also clears the overlay when you are back in the main menu. It stays off unless you turn it on.
onboarding.detect.privacy: To do that it reads the game's own window — not your screen, not any other window — a few times a second while the game is running. The picture never leaves this PC: nothing is saved to disk, nothing is uploaded, and the only thing kept is which map it matched.
onboarding.detect.tab.body: Experimental, and off unless you turn it on: hold your map key in game and the possible locations appear on the game's own big map — the one with your position on it.
onboarding.detect.tab.key: Your map key is {key}. If the game uses a different one, change it under Settings → Overlay.
onboarding.detect.tab.needsMarkers: This needs Show markers, which is switched off on the previous step — there would be nothing to draw.
onboarding.detect.tab.privacy: While this is on and the game is the window in front, the app asks Windows whether that one key is held right now. It never receives, records or sees any other key, it does not take the key away from the game, and nothing is stored or sent.
onboarding.done.title: That is everything
onboarding.done.body: The rest lives under Settings in the menu bar: the overlay's position, size and opacity, every hotkey, the language and the OBS window. FAQ next to it answers the questions this tour skipped.
onboarding.done.network: This app makes two kinds of request and no others: it asks GitHub whether a newer version exists, and whether new or corrected maps exist. Nothing about you or your PC is ever sent, and both can be switched off under Settings → General.
onboarding.done.reopen: You can open this tour again at any time from Settings → General → Show the welcome tour.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.fullscreen.q: The overlay does not show over the game
faq.fullscreen.a: Set Halloween: The Game to Borderless Windowed in its video settings — that is the mode the overlay is built for. The overlay is an always-on-top window, so the game has to be a window too; and a game window with a border or a title bar also stops the markers being drawn on the game's own map.
faq.ban.q: Can the app get me banned?
faq.ban.a: It only displays image files that ship with it. It never reads the game's memory, never injects anything and never touches the game process in any way.
faq.screenshots.a: Only if you switch Auto-detect map on, and it is off by default. While it is on and the game is running, the app captures the game's own window — not your screen, not any other window — about every 0.7 seconds. While the game is not running it only checks every 2 seconds whether that window has appeared yet, and captures nothing. It compares that image, on your own computer, against small thumbnails of the in-game maps that ship inside the app. Nothing is saved to disk and nothing is uploaded: the only thing kept is which map it matched. Switch it off and nothing is captured at all. With markers on the in-game map also on there are a few more of those captures while you are holding your map key: with the key trigger, one when you press it plus a twice-a-second check while the markers are actually up; without it, every 0.45 s and about six times a second while they are up. Separately, the hotkey setting Only while the game is in the foreground looks once a second at the list of open windows and reads, for each one, its program name, its window title, its size and whether it has the keyboard — no pixels, nothing captured and nothing kept.
faq.keyboard.a: It reads one key, and only with markers on the in-game map switched on — which is off by default — and the game running. Switching that mode on makes the app check once that Windows lets it ask at all; that check reads no key. After that, each time, it first asks Windows which program owns the window you are working in; if that is not the game it stops there and no key is read at all. If it is the game, it asks "is the map key held right now?": the one key you set under Game's map key, plus Alt while that key is held, so Alt + Tab is not mistaken for you opening the map. There is no keyboard hook — the app does not receive keystrokes, cannot see what you type, and never asks about any other key. Nothing is written down except that your map key went down or came up. It does not reserve the key either, so the game still sees every press. Pressing it is also never enough on its own: a press only makes the app look at the game's window, and the markers appear only if what it sees really is the map screen. Switch that mode off, or switch on Do not read the key state, and nothing is read at all. Everything else the app does with the keyboard is its own hotkeys, which you choose and can unbind.
faq.internet.a: For two things, both of them a plain request for a public file on GitHub and nothing else. Updates: at startup it asks whether a newer version of this app has been released. New maps: at startup, and then at most once a day, it asks whether new or corrected map images exist — the maps that ship inside the app never change on their own, but the game gets new ones. No accounts, no telemetry, no analytics, nothing about you or your PC is sent either time. Each has its own switch under Settings → General, and with both off the app makes no network requests at all.
faq.newMaps.a: The game gets new maps more often than this app gets a release, so each map is downloaded separately: a few hundred KB of image and detection data, checked against a published checksum before it is stored, instead of a 90 MB app update. It appears in the gallery straight away — no restart — and auto-detect learns it at the same moment. A download that is incomplete or does not match its checksum is thrown away whole and the map you already had is left alone. Turn it off under Settings → General → Check for new maps.
faq.updates.a: When a newer version exists it is downloaded quietly in the background, and then a green banner appears at the top of this window. Nothing is installed until you press Restart and update there (or in the tray menu). The app then closes and a small window in the app's own colours takes its place, showing the steps and a progress bar; it works the disk for a few seconds, and then the app reopens by itself. The installer runs at low priority, so the rest of the PC stays responsive while it unpacks. If that window cannot start for any reason, the plain Windows installer runs instead — the update still happens. You are not asked anything and Windows does not prompt for permission — it installs only for your own user account. Press Later and the banner goes away for now; the update stays waiting for the next time you start the app. Closing or quitting the app never installs anything. The check itself only runs at startup, so if the app has been open for a while, Settings → General → Check for updates now asks again on the spot — the same single request, and it works even with the startup switch off.
faq.updates.a2: If an update still drags, what is left is usually your antivirus reading every unpacked file. Adding %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Halloween Map Overlay to the exclusions under Windows Security → Virus & threat protection → Manage settings → Exclusions removes that cost.
faq.autodetect.a: Switch Auto-detect map on above the gallery, then press Tab in the game once at the start of a match. The overlay switches to that map and names it for a few seconds. It only switches when the map it sees is not the one already on the overlay, so a map you picked by hand is never replaced by itself — and it does follow the game again as soon as a different map comes up. Press {clear} to clear the map and make it forget what it saw, so the next Tab press detects the same map again. When the game goes back to its main menu the overlay clears itself, whether auto-detect or you put that map there — but a map you pick while the menu is already on screen is left alone, so choosing the next map between matches is never undone. Turn that off under Settings → General.
faq.inTheWay.q: The overlay is in the way
faq.inTheWay.a: Press {toggle} to hide it, {opacityUp} / {opacityDown} to change its opacity, {sizeUp} / {sizeDown} to resize it, or move it under Settings → Overlay.
faq.obs.q: How do I record it in OBS?
faq.obs.a: Press Open OBS window, then capture that window in OBS and key out the green background with a chroma-key filter.
faq.customMaps.q: Can I add my own map images?
faq.customMaps.a: Yes — Add custom image in the menu. They appear in the gallery under the Custom creator.
